title: Habitat sheet: desert, pond, woodland, polar
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Properties of materials and habitats (Alchemy Island and Living Things and Their Habitats)
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 16 (Habitat sheet: desert, pond, woodland, polar (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 16: Adaptation: suited to a habitat. To understand that living things have features that suit them to their habitat

questions.q: Why does a polar bear have thick fur?
questions.a: To keep warm in the freezing Arctic.
questions.model: What is the habitat like? Very cold. What does the bear need? Warmth. Thick fur traps warm air. So thick fur keeps it warm.

questions.a: Colours that help a living thing hide.

questions.q: Why would a camel struggle in the Arctic?
questions.a: It is adapted to heat, not freezing cold and snow.

questions.q: Core: Choose a habitat (desert, pond, woodland or polar). Pick one animal and one plant and list two adaptations each.
questions.a: For example: desert: camel (wide feet, stores fat), cactus (spines, thick waxy stem).
questions.model: Teacher does one first: pond, duck: webbed feet (swimming), waterproof feathers (stays dry).

questions.q: Extend: Explain one adaptation in full: feature, condition, how it helps.
questions.a: For example: A cactus has spines instead of leaves because the desert is dry; spines lose less water.

questions.q: Stretch: Design an imaginary animal for a cold, windy mountain and explain three adaptations (no drawing of people).
questions.a: Accept reasoned features, e.g. thick fur, short ears, strong grip.

questions.q: A feature that helps survival is an...
Big question: why can a camel live in the desert but a polar bear cannot?
questions.a: Each is adapted to its own habitat: the camel to heat and dryness, the bear to cold.
